assertions.description: WebTransportError is exposed as a constructor in secure Window contexts.
new WebTransportError() yields name "WebTransportError", legacy code 0, message "", source "stream" and a null streamErrorCode, and is a DOMException.
The standard (message, options) constructor sets message, source "session" and a streamErrorCode above 8 bits (70000).
A string first argument alone selects the standard overload and becomes the message (source defaults to "stream").
assertions.test: (()=>{const e=new WebTransportError('reset by peer');return e.message==='reset by peer'&&e.source==='stream'&&e.streamErrorCode===null;})()

assertions.description: An options.source outside the WebTransportErrorSource enum throws TypeError, while a valid "session" source is accepted.
assertions.test: (()=>{let ok=false;try{ok=new WebTransportError('x',{source:'session'}).source==='session';}catch(e){return false;}if(!ok)return false;try{new WebTransportError('x',{source:'bogus'});return false;}catch(e){return e instanceof TypeError;}})()

assertions.description: options.streamErrorCode is [Clamp] unsigned long: 2^33 clamps to 4294967295 and -5 clamps to 0.
structuredClone() of a WebTransportError returns a new WebTransportError with the same message, source and streamErrorCode.
Serialization keeps a null streamErrorCode null (not 0) and keeps source "stream".
A WebTransportError posted through a MessageChannel arrives as a WebTransportError with its source and streamErrorCode.
assertions.test: new Promise((resolve)=>{const ch=new MessageChannel();const t=setTimeout(()=>resolve(false),2000);ch.port2.onmessage=(ev)=>{clearTimeout(t);const d=ev.data;resolve(d instanceof WebTransportError&&d.source==='session'&&d.streamErrorCode===42);ch.port1.close();ch.port2.close();};ch.port2.onmessageerror=()=>{clearTimeout(t);resolve(false);};try{ch.port1.postMessage(new WebTransportError('pm',{source:'session',streamErrorCode:42}));}catch(e){clearTimeout(t);resolve(false);}})
